I'm now diving deeper into the line retention logic. It seems my initial hypothesis about only keeping horizontal lines was incorrect, and that there's more at play than just orientation. I've made a breakthrough! Examining Example 3 reveals a crucial pattern. All *retained* lines are backslash diagonals (down-right, positive slope). Conversely, the removed lines include vertical, horizontal, and slash diagonals. This strongly suggests that the orientation of the line is the deciding factor in its retention, not necessarily its length.


**Examining Example Line Counts**

I'm now counting line occurrences across the examples. It seems the count of lines with the same orientation might be important. In Example 3, only one backslash diagonal was present, so it was retained. Example 1 had horizontal lines which were retained. Example 2 is peculiar. Lines are split, either having two vertical lines or down-left lines being kept. This seems to suggest that line counts of an orientation, not just the orientation itself, is relevant.


**Verifying Max Count Pattern**

Okay, I've got it! I'm verifying the "maximum count" rule. In Example 1, horizontal lines were most frequent. Example 3 retained diagonal down-right lines, which were also most frequent. In Example 2, vertical AND diagonal down-left lines were the most frequent, and BOTH were retained. I'm now testing the rule on a new input; I see it contains vertical lines only, and I can confirm that they are the maximum-count lines!
